methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Direct commentary on data centers increasing the urban-rural divide signals concentration of infrastructure benefits in Northern Virginia while rural areas bear environmental costs without capability building, reinforcing neither depth nor distribution outside metro cores.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-backed community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia signals potential for distributed capability building through local ownership and peer networks in a historically underserved region, targeting depth through participatory design rather than platform delivery.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates AI education infrastructure in Richmond's university ecosystem, deepening metro capability but requiring intentional distribution mechanisms to prevent this from becoming another excellence pocket isolated from rural regions.

signals.title: Why Darden Is Moving AI Into the Core MBA Experience - Darden Report Online
signals.signal_reading: Darden integrating AI into core MBA curriculum deepens elite business leadership capability in Charlottesville/NoVA networks, but concentrates strategic AI fluency in an already-advantaged corridor rather than distributing across Virginia's workforce.

signals.title: Trump EO impacts new artificial intelligence laws in Virginia - WVTF
signals.signal_reading: Trump executive order impacting Virginia's AI laws signals top-down regulatory shifts that may favor platform-provider compliance frameworks over locally-tailored depth, pushing toward shallow, vendor-mediated adoption patterns statewide.
